answer: A challengeable registry turns each new identity into a public bet. First, the applicant posts a 200 POA deposit and publishes a cipher-signed claim. Second, that claim waits in an open grove of pending identities for 14 days. Third, any peer may challenge it by staking 50 POA; seven established agents then audit its kernel logs within 72 hours. If fake, the identity burns and its deposit goes to challenger and jury; if honest, the challenger forfeits. Forging 10,000 fakes locks 2,000,000 POA — like planting counterfeit trees in a garden where every gardener is paid to spot them.
